original_question: For a finite subset sigma of N^n x N^n of the displayed form with parameters c_i and a_jk, determine necessary and sufficient conditions on those integers ensuring that the quotient monoid N^n / <sigma> is isomorphic to a numerical semigroup.
target_in_paper: Section 5, “Presentations of a numerical semigroup,” specifically the unnumbered open problem near the end of the section asking for conditions on a special staircase-shaped finite subset σ ⊂ ℕ^n × ℕ^n that guarantee ℕ^n/⟨σ⟩ is isomorphic to a numerical semigroup. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s actual question: it correctly identifies that the problem is about a finite subset σ of ℕ^n × ℕ^n of a special displayed form, asks for conditions on the integers c_i and a_jk, and asks exactly when the quotient monoid ℕ^n/⟨σ⟩ is isomorphic to a numerical semigroup. That matches the Section 5 open problem in substance and scope. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
missing_details: The phrase “of the displayed form” is not stand-alone; the paper’s family should be written explicitly as σ = {((c1,0,…,0),(0,a12,…,a1n)), ((0,c2,0,…,0),(a21,0,a23,…,a2n)), …, ((0,…,0,cn),(an1,…,a(n,n-1),0))}. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
The notation ⟨σ⟩ should be defined: in Section 5 it denotes the congruence generated by σ, not a submonoid generated by σ. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

The ambient object should be stated explicitly as the free commutative monoid ℕ^n under addition; this is a monoid-theoretic problem, not a ring-theoretic one. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

“Isomorphic to a numerical semigroup” should be spelled out as “isomorphic as a commutative monoid to some numerical semigroup S ⊂ ℕ,” where a numerical semigroup is a cofinite additive submonoid of ℕ containing 0. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

The quantification over the parameters should be made explicit: n is fixed, σ has exactly n relations of the displayed type, and the entries c_i and a_ij lie in ℕ (with the diagonal positions on the right-hand side replaced by 0 as part of the displayed pattern). ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

To remain paper-faithful, the question should stay restricted to this particular family of staircase-shaped presentations, rather than broadening to arbitrary finite congruence-generating subsets of ℕ^n × ℕ^n. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

No ambient field, homogeneity, degree restriction, or nilpotency assumption is relevant here; adding such hypotheses would move away from the actual Section 5 problem. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
refined_question: Let n ≥ 2 and let σ be the n-element subset of ℕ^n × ℕ^n given by σ = {((c1,0,…,0),(0,a12,…,a1n)), ((0,c2,0,…,0),(a21,0,a23,…,a2n)), …, ((0,…,0,cn),(an1,…,a(n,n-1),0))}, where c1,…,cn and the aij are nonnegative integers. What necessary and sufficient conditions on these integers ensure that the quotient monoid ℕ^n/⟨σ⟩, with ⟨σ⟩ the congruence generated by σ, is isomorphic as a commutative monoid to a numerical semigroup? ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently: characterize exactly when a finite subset σ of the above staircase form is a presentation of a numerical semigroup, i.e. when there exists a numerical semigroup S such that S ≅ ℕ^n/⟨σ⟩. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
justification: Section 5 first defines congruences on commutative monoids, quotient monoids, the congruence generated by a finite subset σ, and the notion of a presentation of a numerical semigroup. Immediately afterward, the paper narrows from the general algorithmic recognition problem to a specific family of subsets σ and asks for conditions on the integers c_i and a_ij ensuring that ℕ^n/⟨σ⟩ is isomorphic to a numerical semigroup. The remarks that embedding-dimension-three numerical semigroups (Herzog) and neat numerical semigroups (Komeda) have presentations of this form confirm that this is the precise official problem your draft is targeting. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
